note: Weekly S.O.A.P. devotional (Mon) — Scripture · Observation · Application · Prayer. Aligned to the quarterly series in 09-LOTL-52-week-calendar.md.

devotionals.title: New Beginnings Start With Mercy
devotionals.verse: The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
devotionals.observation: Lamentations was written from the ruins of Jerusalem — everything fallen. In the middle of the ashes, the poet stops and insists: God's love has not stopped, and every single morning starts a fresh supply of mercy.
devotionals.application: If yesterday was a failure, it is already out of mercy budget — a new morning has started a new supply. Write down one honest 'start again' for today: one apology, one new habit, one step toward God.
devotionals.prayer: Father, thank You that Your mercies are new this morning. I bring You yesterday without shame and today without fear. Give me strength for one new beginning.

devotionals.title: Mercy Is A Promise, Not A Feeling
devotionals.verse: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love. He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities... as far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us.
devotionals.observation: God's mercy is described with a distance you can never cross twice — east from west. It means your sin and you are permanently separated, not because you deserved it but because He chose mercy.
devotionals.application: The day you repent, mercy is already waiting — it never 'runs out of stock'. This week, receive mercy for your own failure and then extend the same one-time no-replay forgiveness to someone who hurt you.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, thank You for a mercy that outlasts my mistakes. Teach me to receive it without suspicion and to give it without resentment.

devotionals.title: Restore The Years
devotionals.verse: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the hopper, the destroyer, and the cutter, my great army, which I sent among you.
devotionals.observation: The locusts — small, many, devouring — take what took years to grow. But God promises restoration of the years themselves, not just the crops. Time you thought was wasted is recoverable with Him.
devotionals.application: Where has life eaten your years — a wasted season, an illness, a wrong choice? Restore means what the enemy stole is not lost forever. Name one 'locust' area and begin rebuilding it this month with one small faithful step.
devotionals.prayer: God of restoration, take back what the locusts ate in my life. Rebuild my wasted seasons and let my years count double for Your glory.

devotionals.title: Frustration Is An Invitation
devotionals.verse: The Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.
devotionals.observation: When nothing works and everything frustrates, the psalm does not promise the problem leaves instantly. It promises the Lord draws near to the crushed. Frustration is a signal your soul is tired — not a proof God left.
devotionals.application: Treat frustration as a warning light, not a verdict. Stop, breathe, send a short honest prayer ('Lord, I am stuck'), and take the one small next step that is in your power today. Movement restores faith faster than thinking.
devotionals.prayer: Father, You are near even when my plans are not. I release the frustration in my hands and take the next small step in faith. Send Your peace that passes understanding.
